title: Site-to-site VPN with IKEv2
blurb: Build an IKEv2 crypto map tunnel between two branch routers, from proposal to verification.
purpose: Sites need to share private traffic over the Internet without exposing it. This lab builds a classic crypto-map site-to-site VPN with IKEv2 and strong algorithms, piece by piece, so you see what each part of the configuration does. It covers VPN fundamentals from the Network Security domain.
scenario: Headquarters LAN **10.1.1.0/24** sits behind R1, whose outside interface **GigabitEthernet0/0** is **203.0.113.1**. The branch LAN **10.2.2.0/24** sits behind R2 at **198.51.100.2**. R2 is already configured. Build R1's side of an IKEv2 site-to-site tunnel with a pre-shared key **S2SVpnKey**, AES-256, SHA-256 and DH group 19.
objectives: Know what IKE and ESP need from the path
Define the IKEv2 proposal, policy, keyring and profile
Define the IPsec transform set and interesting traffic
Tie everything together in a crypto map on the outside interface

steps.title: Open the path
steps.learn: IKE negotiates the tunnel, and ESP carries the encrypted data. A firewall in the path has to allow both, and with NAT in the path (NAT-T), everything moves to UDP 4500.
steps.task: Pick everything a firewall between R1 and R2 must allow for this VPN, assuming there's no NAT in the path.
steps.question: What must be allowed between 203.0.113.1 and 198.51.100.2?

options.why: AH isn't used here. The transform set uses ESP, and AH can't cross NAT anyway.
That's TLS, used by SSL VPNs such as AnyConnect, not by IPsec site-to-site.

steps.title: IKEv2 proposal and policy
steps.learn: The **proposal** lists the algorithms for the IKE SA itself: encryption, integrity and the Diffie-Hellman group. Group 19 is 256-bit elliptic curve. The **policy** says which proposals to offer.
steps.task: Create proposal **PROP-1** with **aes-cbc-256**, integrity **sha256** and DH group **19**, and a policy **POL-1** that uses it.
steps.hint: `crypto ikev2 proposal PROP-1`, then `encryption aes-cbc-256`, `integrity sha256`, `group 19`. Then `crypto ikev2 policy POL-1` and `proposal PROP-1`.

commands.explain: Creates an IKEv2 proposal, the set of algorithms offered to the peer.
Uses AES-256 to encrypt the IKE session.
Uses SHA-256 to check integrity.
Uses Diffie-Hellman group 19 (256-bit elliptic curve) for the key exchange.
Creates an IKEv2 policy that says which proposals to use.

commands.note: R1 will offer AES-256, SHA-256 and group 19 for the IKE SA.
commands.explain: Attaches the PROP-1 proposal to the policy.

steps.title: Keyring
steps.learn: A **keyring** stores the pre-shared key for each peer. In IKEv2, each side can even use a different key in each direction.
steps.task: Create keyring **KR** with peer **R2** at **198.51.100.2** and pre-shared key **S2SVpnKey**.

commands.explain: Creates a keyring to hold pre-shared keys.
Adds an entry for the peer R2.
Sets R2's public address.
Sets the pre-shared key for R2. It must match on both sides.

steps.title: IKEv2 profile
steps.learn: The **profile** decides which peer it applies to and how both sides prove who they are.
steps.task: Create profile **PROF-R2**: match the remote identity address **198.51.100.2 255.255.255.255**, use **pre-share** for both local and remote authentication, and use keyring **KR**.
steps.hint: `crypto ikev2 profile PROF-R2`, `match identity remote address 198.51.100.2 255.255.255.255`, `authentication remote pre-share`, `authentication local pre-share`, `keyring local KR`.

commands.explain: Creates an IKEv2 profile, which ties identity and authentication together.
Uses this profile when the peer is 198.51.100.2.
Expects the peer to authenticate with a pre-shared key.
Authenticates this router to the peer with a pre-shared key.
Uses keyring KR for the keys.

steps.title: Transform set and interesting traffic
steps.learn: The **transform set** chooses the algorithms for the IPsec (child) SAs that carry the data. The **crypto ACL** marks the traffic that should be encrypted. R2's ACL must be the mirror image of R1's.
steps.task: Create transform set **TS** with **esp-aes 256** and **esp-sha256-hmac** in **tunnel** mode. Then create extended ACL **VPN-TRAFFIC** that permits IP from **10.1.1.0/24** to **10.2.2.0/24**.
steps.hint: `crypto ipsec transform-set TS esp-aes 256 esp-sha256-hmac`, `mode tunnel`, then `ip access-list extended VPN-TRAFFIC` and `permit ip 10.1.1.0 0.0.0.255 10.2.2.0 0.0.0.255`.

commands.cmd: crypto ipsec transform-set TS esp-aes 256 esp-sha256-hmac
commands.explain: Defines how data is protected: ESP with AES-256 encryption and SHA-256 integrity.
Uses tunnel mode, which protects the whole original IP packet.
Creates an ACL to define which traffic goes into the VPN.

commands.note: Traffic from the HQ LAN to the branch LAN will be encrypted.
commands.explain: Selects traffic from the local LAN 10.1.1.0/24 to the remote LAN 10.2.2.0/24.

steps.title: Crypto map
steps.learn: The **crypto map** ties it all together: the peer, the transform set, the IKEv2 profile and the ACL. It does nothing until it's applied to the interface that faces the peer.
steps.task: Create crypto map **CMAP** sequence **10** (ipsec-isakmp): peer **198.51.100.2**, transform set **TS**, IKEv2 profile **PROF-R2**, match address **VPN-TRAFFIC**. Apply it to **GigabitEthernet0/0**.
steps.hint: `crypto map CMAP 10 ipsec-isakmp`, `set peer 198.51.100.2`, `set transform-set TS`, `set ikev2-profile PROF-R2`, `match address VPN-TRAFFIC`, then `interface GigabitEthernet0/0` and `crypto map CMAP`.

commands.output:
% NOTE: This new crypto map will remain disabled until a peer
        and a valid access list have been configured.
commands.explain: Creates crypto map CMAP entry 10, which ties all the parts together.
Sets the VPN peer.
Uses transform set TS.
Uses the IKEv2 profile PROF-R2.
Encrypts traffic that matches VPN-TRAFFIC.
Enters the Internet-facing interface.

commands.note: The crypto map is live on the outside interface.
commands.explain: Applies the crypto map, which turns the VPN on for this interface.

steps.title: Verify the tunnel
steps.learn: The first packet from 10.1.1.0/24 to 10.2.2.0/24 triggers the negotiation. A status of **READY** means the IKE SA is up. The IPsec SA counters show packets being encrypted and decrypted.
steps.task: Display the IKEv2 security associations, then the IPsec security associations.
steps.hint: `do show crypto ikev2 sa` and `do show crypto ipsec sa`.

summary: An IKEv2 proposal, policy, keyring and profile with a pre-shared key, an AES-256/SHA-256 transform set, a crypto ACL for the two LANs, and a crypto map applied to the outside interface, verified with the IKEv2 and IPsec SA tables.
